reasoning: The benchmark transcription asks for an unbounded image on a bounded subset of ℝ. Every such set is totally bounded, and a uniformly continuous function has totally bounded, hence bounded, image there. The original Lean statement quantifies over every set E. Taking E = ∅ refutes it because every image of ∅ is bounded. Rudin’s second sentence asks what happens when boundedness of the domain is omitted. The identity on all of ℝ gives the required counterexample because it is uniformly continuous and has unbounded image.
